episodes.178552: Diurnal heating, convergence along surface boundaries, and an unstable atmosphere contributed to scattered late afternoon and evening thunderstorms.  A few produced small hail.
episodes.178564: Thunderstorms moved across the Gulf waters, producing marine thunderstorm wind gusts.
episodes.178565: A squall line developed over northwestern Kansas during the late morning of the 9th, and translated southeast across the state during the day. The line of storms moved into northeastern Oklahoma during the evening. The strongest storm in the line produced 59 mph wind gusts.
episodes.178567: A cluster of thunderstorms moved across the area, producing flash flooding and a funnel cloud.
episodes.178570: Accelerated snowmelt from a near-record snowpack due to above normal temperatures produced high and fast flow on drainages in La Plata County. As a result, flooding compromised The Oxbow Preserve along the Animas River.
episodes.178578: A band of thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours in northwest into central Alabama, which lifted slowly northeast during the early evening hours.  Very heavy downpours resulted in flash flooding in parts of northwest Alabama, including the Florence area. Rainfall amounts reached 3-5 inches in a few isolated locations. A gust front produced strong and gusty winds in parts of north central Alabama in Morgan and Madison Counties, knocking a few trees down in Harvest. A few storms became severe within this outflow producing damaging microbursts as well.
episodes.178587: A strong upper level storm system accompanied by a strong portion of the jetstream brought high winds to portions of central and eastern NM. These southwest winds reached nearly the entire state with high wind gusts being reported from Santa Fe to Albuquerque and through the highlands from Las Vegas to Clines Corners and Vaughn. Areas of blowing dust resulted from these winds, slightly dropping visibilities. The high winds also aided in the rapid spread of a new wildfire near Sapello, NM during the afternoon. There were no reports of damage or injuries directly related to the high winds. Meanwhile, severe weather broke out across far eastern NM along the TX border during the afternoon and evening hours. Thunderstorm activity favored a dryline feature with individual storm cells producing mostly pea to nickel size hail and severe wind gusts. Several severe wind gusts were reported in portions of northeastern NM with one report of one inch size hail near Clovis. Nickel size hail was also reported in San Jon, NM. There were no reports of wind or hail damage.
episodes.178608: An upper trough moved across Central California on May 9. This system provided for enough instability for scattered thunderstorms to break out along the West Side Hills and the Sierra Nevada during the afternoon. One thunderstorm produced heavy rainfall near Coalinga which resulted in a brief closure of SR 198 just to the southwest of Coalinga as rocks and mud impacted the highway.
episodes.178635: Severe thunderstorms with large hail developed across Adams, Boulder, Denver, Larimer, Morgan and Weld counties.  The hail ranged from 1.0 to 2.5 inches in diameter.  Extensive damage to homes and vehicles was reported in Longmont, Erie, Johnstown and Firestone.   The largest hail occurred in Morgan County, where tennis ball size hail was reported.
episodes.178742: Isolated thunderstorms and showers across central and eastern Nevada, caused gusty outflow winds.
episodes.178804: Scattered strong to locally severe thunderstorms developed across far southeast Wyoming during the early evening hours on 5/9.
episodes.178806: A line of severe thunderstorms swept across the western Nebraska Panhandle during the late afternoon and early evening hours on 5/9, primarily producing damaging straight line winds. A separate round of isolated storms impacted the same areas during the late evening and overnight hours into 5/10, with numerous reports of hail and flash flooding in and around Scottsbluff and Gering.
episodes.179299: Storms developed over the central Plains near the Kansas and Nebraska border during the afternoon of the 7th and moved southeastward across central and south central Missouri from the pre-dawn hours to the early morning of the 8th. These storms left an outflow boundary over central Missouri that sparked a second round of storms during the afternoon. These storms were much stronger and produced hail across central Missouri through the evening of the  8th. The strongest storm produced hail to the size of baseballs in Dent County near Stone Hill. Rainfall amounts over two inches occurred with these storms near Nevada, Lake of the Ozarks, and north of Salem.
episodes.179307: Severe storms developed over far southwest Missouri and southeast Kansas during the early morning of the 9th as a low level jet interacted with a stalled front along the northwest Arkansas and northeast Oklahoma border. These storms dissipated during the late morning, but left another outflow boundary that interacted with an approaching storm complex to produce another round of strong to severe storms during the afternoon and evening of the 9th. Numerous reports of quarter to golf ball sized hail and wind gusts over 60 mph were reported over southwest Missouri and southeast Kansas.
episodes.179308: Showers and storms persistent over the region as moisture was pulled northward ahead of an upper level low that moved northward from central Texas into western Missouri. There were a few reports of severe hail and wind damage, but overall less severe weather than the previous few days. Rainfall accumulations of one to two inches occurred mainly south of I-44 and east of I-49.
episodes.179405: Afternoon sea breeze thunderstorms produce severe hail near Bronson in Levy County.
episodes.179537: Thunderstorms initially developed along a warm front over southwestern North Dakota during the late afternoon and early evening hours. One storm strengthened and became a supercell near the border of Mercer and Morton counties. The storm then moved towards the Bismarck and Mandan areas, with multiple reports of golf ball size hail along its path. The storm continued to produce golf ball size hail in Mandan and the west end of Bismarck, before it weakened as it moved through Burleigh County. Storm damage estimates were around one and a half million dollars. Additional storms then formed later in the evening, with one of those producing golf ball size hail in Kidder County.
episodes.179555: An isolated strong storm developed along a boundary in northeast South Dakota. This cell produced hail up to 1 inch.
episodes.179706: A cold front sagged into Eastern NC during the afternoon hours. An unstable atmosphere with strong shear in place ahead of the front primed the region for severe thunderstorm development. The timing of the front coincided with peak afternoon heating, allowing for multiple rounds of supercells that produced scattered to numerous severe storm reports during the mid afternoon hours all the way through the mid evening hours. Hail up to two inches in diameter, and wind gusts of 60 to 70 mph occurred with the strongest thunderstorms. The severe hail fell all the way to the coast, which is quite rare.
episodes.179826: During the afternoon hours, scattered storms developed over Northwest Kansas as a warm front moved north. These storms produced hail ranging from pea to golf ball in size and a brief tornado near the town of Selden. The largest hail fell near the towns of Selden, Levant, and Edson. Heavy rain with amounts up to  five inches produced flash flooding over portions of Thomas and Sheridan counties. These storms also produced strong winds with gusts up to 81 mph reported. The peak gust occurred just south of Selden, Kansas.
episodes.179950: A mesoscale convective system developed across north central Kansas during the morning hours of May 9th, 2023.  This complex of storms moved east-southeast across central and southeast Kansas, producing damaging wind gusts of 65 to 75 mph and large hail of 1.5 to 2 inches in diameter.  Additional severe storms developed behind the complex of storms during the late afternoon and evening hours and moved across south central Kansas.
episodes.179967: An outflow boundary from a decaying MCS triggered isolated strong to severe thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening hours on May 9th. Due to the slow movement of the storms, some localized flooding also occurred.
episodes.180206: A backdoor cool front moved NE to SW across the local forecast in the afternoon. Convergence near this front and the inland progressing east coast sea breeze front over a moist and diurnally unstable airmass triggered strong to isolated severe storms.
episodes.180207: A cluster of thunderstorms developed across portions of southeast South Carolina in the early evening hours and tracked toward the coast. These thunderstorms produced several reports of strong damaging wind gusts and large hail.
episodes.180210: Strong thunderstorms developed inland across Berkeley and Charleston counties in the evening hours. These thunderstorms eventually progressed to the coast, producing strong wind gusts along the coast and in Charleston Harbor.
episodes.180507: Numerous severe thunderstorms developed southwest of Denver and pushed north-northeast through the metro area. The storms produced extensive hail, ranging from quarter to tennis ball size.  As the storms move northeast onto the plains, the hail increase in size from baseball to softball size.  In addition, the storm produced several tornadoes as they move across Morgan and Washington counties.   Southeast of Brush, an EF1 tornado touched down and caused extensive damage to a residence.  Part of the roof was torn off the residence. The nearby barn had a portion of its roof ripped off the building. Some wood storage buildings were destroyed and trees on the property were uprooted. The two elderly residence in the home at the time were not injured.  Several other weaker tornadoes touched down in Washington County but no damage was observed.
episodes.180541: During the afternoon hours a cluster of storms developed over Northwest Kansas, moving northwest into Yuma County. As the storms approached the eastern side of the city of Wray large hail ranging from the size of quarters to baseballs fell.
episodes.180560: Thunderstorms formed along a warm front, situated along the Kansas/Nebraska border during the late afternoon hours of May 10th. As this activity lifted north of the front, it became severe with large hail. Golf ball sized hail was reported in southern Chase County.
episodes.180630: A lone supercell developed near the Davis Mountains and tracked northeast along the Pecos River Valley.
episodes.180656: Thunderstorms trained over the eastern parts of San Patricio County during the afternoon on the 9th and over Aransas and eastern Calhoun Counties on the morning of the 10th. The storms produced very heavy rainfall with amounts between 3 to 5 inches. The heavy rainfall caused flooding in Aransas Pass, Rockport, and Port Lavaca.
episodes.180662: A ridge of high pressure over the middle of the country provided days of dry weather, and monthly rainfall deficits exceeded two inches at Little Rock (Pulaski County). A lifting warm front that retreated back into the far northeastern part of Arkansas as a stationary front brought several, afternoon rounds of pulse severe thunderstorms with hail and damaging winds to the area, including a brief tornado.
episodes.180688: Scattered thunderstorms occurred over south-central Texas into the Brush Country during the afternoon and evening of the 9th. A severe thunderstorm formed south of Choke Canyon Reservoir and moved to the southwest of George West. Quarter sized hail was reported southwest of George West.
episodes.180834: Numerous thunderstorms moved through portions of southwest Kansas.
episodes.180888: A series of upper disturbances pushed across South Louisiana producing daily scattered thunderstorms. A few storms became severe during the period of the 6th through the 10th. A tornado also developed in Acadia Parish causing damage near Morse.
episodes.180984: A closed low propagated from SW CONUS and rapidly intensified over the southeast Colorado plains. A combination of strong lift due to the rapidly intensifying cyclone and orographic lift created heavy snow over the mountains. Since this was a late spring system with origins from the Pacific, the lower elevations were warm enough for heavy rainfall that ended up causing some flooding issues along the Fountain Creek in El Paso County and Pueblo County.
episodes.181000: A storm system moved into the area on the morning of the May 9, producing widespread heavy rain and some flash flooding through the morning of May 10.
episodes.181086: An upper level low generated thunderstorms in a warm, moist airmass. Some of these storms produced locally heavy rain leading to local flooding.
episodes.181088: Slow-moving bands of showers and thunderstorms associated with an upper low located over the Lower Mississippi Valley intensified during the afternoon hours on May 10, 2023, when instability peaked. There were isolated reports of large hail and a few microbursts occurred resulting in damaging winds.
episodes.181089: Slow-moving bands of showers and thunderstorms associated with an upper low located over the Lower Mississippi Valley intensified during the afternoon hours on May 10, 2023, when instability peaked. There were isolated reports of large hail and a few microbursts occurred resulting in damaging winds.
episodes.181090: Slow-moving bands of showers and thunderstorms associated with an upper low located over the Lower Mississippi Valley intensified during the afternoon hours on May 10, 2023, when instability peaked. Locally heavy rainfall resulted in isolated flash flooding over extreme northeast Mississippi.
